transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is... I just keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven look around my jaw. It's mostly on one side of my face. I saw myself in all these recent family photos, and it just really stood out to me, and now I can't unsee it. My wife tells me she barely notices anything, and none of my clients at work seem to see it either, but... I just can't stop focusing on it.
How certain are you that the unevenness around your jaw is truly noticeable to other people, despite what your wife tells you?

Well, I guess I'm not entirely certain. I mean, when my wife says she doesn't see it, part of me believes her because she's usually honest with me. But then I look in the mirror or see a photo, and it just seems so obvious to me. So, I don't know... I guess I'm torn. I feel like people must see it, but maybe they're just being polite or not paying as much attention as I am.
How often do you find yourself checking your jaw in mirrors or photographs because of this concern?

Well, it happens a fair amount, especially at work. Before I go into client meetings, I'll usually check the bathroom mirror... and I'll pull out my phone camera several times, too. I try to adjust the lighting, or maybe change how my collar sits, or just practice angling my face so the sagging isn't as obvious. 

And then, even when I'm out or talking to people... I catch myself comparing my face to the younger advisors at the firm, or to people at gallery events my wife and I go to. I'll just be doing that in my head instead of actually focusing on the conversation I'm supposed to be having.
Do you have any other recurring unwanted thoughts or repetitive rituals that are unrelated to your appearance?

No, not really. I mean... I don't have anything else like that going on. It's just this thing with my jaw that I get stuck on. I don't have any other rituals or thoughts that keep popping up about other things.
